Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Zarin Zarin Sultana Senior Customer Success Manager [image: Clever Icon Logo] Visit our Help Center and Clever Academy to learn more about Clever!

Description: Hi Brian, Thank you for taking a prompt look at this. These are great questions that bring up a few key points I would like to clarify: 1. *API v2 Deprecation*: API v2.0 will be deprecated at the beginning of 2028. The updated form reflects Clever Complete—encompassing SSO, Secure Sync, LMS Connect, and AnySchool—and includes the necessary language to make these tools available to our partners. However, partners still choose to adopt these tools at their own pace with no implementation requirements for the new functionality. If you only need Secure Sync rostering, you are welcome to focus solely on that integration. We will continue to support it at the same cost, provided it meets v3 requirements. I will also clarify that Sphero currently remains on the legacy Secure Sync order form, so we may not complete the transition to Clever Complete until the next renewal period. If you'd like to go ahead and transition to the new order form this year or view it, please let me know. Ultimately, we're here to help ensure that Sphero continues to be supported on API v3. Description: Hi Jennifer, I want to flag an issue we are experiencing with Clever on shared classroom devices and request a meeting with your engineering team. When a student logs out of Clever, only the Clever portal session ends. Every app launched through Instant Login, including LINKS, maintains its own session. As a result, the next student using that Chromebook or Mac inherits the previous student's accounts. Because there is no single, back-channel, or front-channel logout mechanism to end all sessions at once, this poses a security risk for us and the school districts. While we are building a workaround extension that clears site data after inactivity, this is only a device-level patch rather than a solution at the identity layer. I would like to speak with an engineer to understand: - If Clever currently has any global sign-out or session-termination capabilities. - If there is an OIDC logout roadmap for partner apps. - If there is a supported method for an app like LINKS to be notified when a Clever session ends. Could you please set up a 30-minute call with someone from your engineering or identity product team within the next week or two? We are happy to share our findings and what we have built so far. Thanks, Ricardo Morales CES LINKS To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to app-success+unsubscribe@clever.com.

Description: *Hi Clever Team,* As we continue to enhance our Clever integration and overall user experience, we have a few questions and would appreciate your guidance. *Current Integration* We currently use *Clever Secure Sync* (rostering API with bearer tokens) to sync students, staff, and classes for our partner schools. We’re also in the certification process to support *Clever SSO* for individual user authentication. *What We’re Trying to Achieve* When a school is archived in our system (for example, due to a contract ending or school closure), we’d like to automatically disconnect that school’s integration with Clever to ensure that: - Data is no longer synced from Clever for that school - The sharing relationship in Clever is properly terminated for security and compliance *Our Current Understanding* Based on our review of Clever’s API documentation, we understand that: - Clever does not currently provide a partner API endpoint to programmatically unshare or disconnect an app from a school - Sharing control resides with district administrators in the Clever dashboard - The Events API can be used to detect when a district unshares a school from our app *Questions* We’d appreciate your guidance on the following: *1. Recommended Approach* What is Clever’s recommended best practice for handling disconnection when a school is archived on a partner platform so we don't get charged for connections that should no longer exist? *2. Events API Setup* - Should we enable the Events API to detect when districts remove sharing? - Which specific event types should we listen for (e.g., schools.updated, schools.deleted)? - What is the process for registering our webhook endpoint with your team? *3. Soft vs. Hard Disconnect* - Do you recommend guiding district admins through a manual unshare process in the Clever dashboard? - Or is there a supported or preferred way for partners to programmatically manage this from their end? *4. Token Management* - When we stop using a bearer token (by removing it from our system), is there a revocation endpoint we should call? - Or is it sufficient to simply stop making API requests? *Our Planned Implementation* Unless advised otherwise, we’re planning to: - Enable Events API webhooks to detect when districts formally unshare schools Thank you for your guidance. Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Description: Hi Layth and Clever Integrations Team, We're reaching out because we've identified an issue with student enrollment dates in the data we receive through the Clever API, and we'd like your help understanding whether this is expected behavior. We consume the enrollments property from the Student object ( roles.student.enrollments) to track when students enroll at their schools. Per Clever's documentation, start_date represents "when a student first enrolled in the school in Clever." However, we're seeing this value change unexpectedly across daily syncs for the same student at the same school. Here are two patterns we've observed across multiple districts: *Example 1: Enrollment disappears and reappears with a new start date* Date Retrieved Enrollment Start Date Enrollment End Date 2025-10-02 2025-08-02 2026-05-22 2025-10-03 2025-08-02 2026-05-22 2025-10-04 *(empty — no enrollment)* ... *(empty for ~35 consecutive days)* 2025-11-07 *(empty)* *2025-11-08* *2025-11-08* *2026-05-22* 2025-11-09 2025-11-08 2026-05-22 The enrollment existed with an August 2 start date, disappeared for over a month, then reappeared with a new start date of November 8. *Example 2: Start date shifts forward on an existing enrollment* Date Retrieved Enrollment Start Date Enrollment End Date 2025-11-11 2025-08-01 0001-01-01 *(no end date)* 2025-11-12 2025-08-01 0001-01-01 *2025-11-13* *2025-11-12* *2026-06-01* 2025-11-14 2025-11-12 2026-06-01 The start date changed from August 1 to November 12 overnight, and an end date appeared where there previously was none. This is impacting our application because we rely on enrollment dates for important business logic such as rostering, reporting, and student timeline tracking. Shifting start dates and temporary gaps in enrollment data undermine the reliability of these features. We'd appreciate your help clarifying a few questions: 1. Is it expected for start_date to change on an existing enrollment record, or should it remain stable once set? 2. Are these changes originating from the SIS data the district provides, or from how Clever processes enrollment records? 3. Can enrollment records temporarily disappear and reappear as part of normal sync behavior? Depending on how this is intended to work on Clever's end, we may need to explore options on our side — such as storing and preserving enrollment dates independently. Before going down that path, though, we'd like to understand the expected behavior so we can determine the best approach together. Happy to provide any additional details, student IDs, or district information that would help with the investigation. Description: Hi Team, We are currently facing an issue while establishing the connection with Clever. At present, our flow relies on the status of the Clever popup window to determine whether the user has successfully connected. Once the popup tab is closed, we make an internal API call to verify the connection status and display the appropriate message to the user. Recently, this flow has started breaking. Upon investigation, we observed that the issue occurs when a new window is opened with a different origin and the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header is set in a way that restricts interaction across origins. Could you please let us know if there have been any recent changes on your end that might have introduced or modified the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy behavior? We’re seeing issues in the OneRoster file that’s being generated, specifically in the or.users.userIds column. Here’s an example : sourcedId,status,dateLastModified,enabledUser,orgSourcedIds,role,username,userIds,givenName,familyName,middleName,identifier,email,sms,phone,agentSourcedIds,grades,password 55b93b243d13b70d00b8ad9a,,,true,55b93b203d13b70d00b8aa33,teacher,lynchjo,"{SisId:18835},{Fed:55b93b243d13b70d00b8ad9a},{TeacherNumber:18835},{StateId:}",Joann,Lynch,,18835,jolynch@dbqschools.org,,,,, As can be seen users.sourceid = 55b93b243d13b70d00b8ad9a has a value in their userIds column of "{SisId:18835},{Fed:55b93b243d13b70d00b8ad9a},{TeacherNumber:18835},{StateId:}" This is defined, in the ORCSV spec (https://www.imsglobal.org/oneroster-v11-final-csv-tables) as (essentially) a list of key/value pairs (the spec refers to them as Type/ID). Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Description: Hi team! We are scoping a significant piece of work on EverTutor and want to check it against Clever before we build. Below is what we are building, what we need from the data, and the questions we have. Some are about the new work and some are housekeeping on our account. Numbered so you can reply against them. What we are building, in three parts: 1. Classes in EverTutor get created automatically from the classrooms we receive through Clever. A teacher signs in and their classes are already there. 2. The students in those classes are managed automatically, in and out. When a student is added to a classroom in the SIS, they appear. When they are removed, they come out. The teacher never maintains it by hand. 3. Teachers can also create their own groups, separate from the rostered ones, and add students into them directly from the district roster. These teacher-made groups stay under the teacher’s control and the sync never changes them. We already do the first two, at least in part. The third is new. What we need from the data: 1. The teacher’s classrooms and the students enrolled in them, which we receive today 2. A reliable signal when a student joins or leaves a classroom, so part two happens without waiting for a full re-sync 3. Access to the wider roster for a school that has been shared with us, so a teacher building their own group has students to pick from 4. Grade level on the student record, so we can narrow that picker to the grade the teacher actually teaches Questions on sharing scope and roster access 1. When a district shares at the school level, do we receive every student in that school, or only students enrolled in classrooms that are shared with us? This is the single question that decides whether part three is possible. For example, Pleasant View Elementary School District shares 290 students with us at one school. Is that the full school roster, or only classroom enrollments? 2. Is grade level reliably populated on the student record, and can a district leave it blank? Our partner dashboard flags missing required fields on students for every district we serve, and we would like to know whether grade is among them. 3. For a teacher who works across more than one school, how is that represented, and do we receive all of their schools? 4. How are staff represented compared with teachers? Several of our districts have principals, aides and interventionists who need the same access a teacher has, and we want to handle them correctly rather than guess. Questions on keeping classes current 5. How does a student being removed from a classroom come through to us? Is it a deleted enrollment, a status flag, or simply an absence from the next sync? 6. How do we tell a real removal apart from a partial or failed sync? If a feed comes through incomplete, we do not want to empty a teacher’s class and lose their setup. Is there anything in the data that signals a sync is complete and safe to act on? 7. How do we learn about joins and leaves between full syncs? Is there an events or change feed available to us, and if so what is the typical lag? Question on teachers who sign up directly 8. If a teacher creates an EverTutor account directly with an email and password, and their district already has a roster shared with us, are we permitted to match that teacher to their roster record and create their classes automatically? If matching on a verified school email is acceptable to you, we would like to know what else you expect us to check. If it is not, we will instead detect the district and prompt the teacher to sign in through Clever to load their classes, and we would rather confirm that with you than guess. Question on data use 9. If a district shares a school with us, are we permitted to show a teacher at that school a list of students who are not in that teacher’s own classrooms, so the teacher can build their own group? This is the one we most want in writing. We will not build part three until we have your position on it. Questions on development and testing 10. Can we have a second Clever application for development, with its own client id and redirect URI? We currently use one application for both development and production, which means we cannot test a sign-in flow without it landing on production. If a second application is not possible, can a single application hold more than one redirect URI that we select at authorization time? 11. How do we test a user who is not shared with us? We pass return_unshared=true and need to verify we show the correct access page rather than creating an empty account. Is there a way to simulate this without asking a real district to change their sharing rules? 12. Who controls sharing on our own #DEMO SigIQ Sandbox district, and can our team get the district-side login? We need to unshare and reshare a student to test how our sync responds, and the partner dashboard is read only for sharing. Housekeeping on our account 13. Perry Public School District shows “1 of 5 licenses”. What does that cap control, what happens if we pass it, and does it limit how many schools can be shared? 14. Pleasant View Elementary School District shows a pending sharing request. What is it waiting on, and what do we need to do to move it along? 15. Perry’s last successful sync was October 8 and today is October 12. Is a 4 day gap normal for an SFTP district, and do we get alerted when a district stops syncing? 16. For the Clever compliance work we have in flight, is there a written checklist of what we need to pass, and a date we should be working back from? If other partners have built something like part three and there are pitfalls worth knowing about, we would welcome the steer. Happy to get on a call if that is easier than working through this in writing. Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Also, students who speak a language other than English at home are usually required to take a test. Subject: [Urgent Action Required] API v2.x Contacts will be sunsetted July 31, 2025
Developer: Column "[Cases: Partner Engineering/Developer]" does not exist
Has Dedicated Support: Column "[Cases: Partner Engineering/Has Dedicated Support]" does not exist
Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Zarin Zarin Sultana Senior Customer Success Manager [image: Clever Icon Logo] Visit our Help Center and Clever Academy to learn more about Clever!

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Description: Hi Ramiro, Thank you for reaching out! For starters, Better Together Cubed already has access to AnySchool. Partner Engineering will confirm exactly what changes, if any, are needed in your authorize and token flow. *A note on ClassLink connections, *SIS connections and CSV/SFTP uploads require no additional work on your side. ClassLink is the exception, connecting ClassLink districts requires becoming a ClassLink certified partner. That certification gets your app into the ClassLink App Library, grants Roster Server API access, and lets you give districts a clear yes when they ask whether you support ClassLink. Here is a guide on getting certified . Two things are worth knowing going into that process. First, certification is scoped to rostering, so the SSO configuration stays on our side and we will support you through it. Second, expect the review to center on your integration architecture and data handling, so it helps to speak to those details in depth. Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. Description: Hi, Amplify has noticed a change made by Clever which has resulted in a poor login experience for our customers using Clever login button on Amplify's login page. Right now, if they click the login with Clever button, a popup opens to complete the process. However, instead of that popup closing when it's complete (as it has in the past), the user now gets logged into our platform *within* the popup. Then, they have to make the screen larger, etc., to move ahead. This also means Amplify will now be open in two windows for them. We are not sure what change was made and think we have a short term mitigation to this but would like to better understand the change that was made, why, and how to avoid any unexpected changes like this moving forward. If helpful, below is what one of our engineers noticed around changes to this login flow: We trigger an oidc flow to Clever from Keycloak by opening a new window up pointing to Keycloak's Clever broker endpoint ( https://my.learning.amplify.com/auth/realms/Amplify/broker/clever/endpoint). This does successfully open up clever in the popup window, but somewhere along the way the hierarchy of the windows is lost. We open these popups in a window we've named KeycloakSignInWindow - with Google (which works fine), when I inspect the popup's window.parent I see that the parent is named 'KeycloakSignInWindow', but when Clever's login page loads up, the parent name is ''. This, from keycloak's perspective, means it no longer thinks that the popup is open, and breaks our post-auth landing page from being able to post a message back to the window opener to state that the login is done and the main page may proceed. -- Joe Rosen Vice President of Product Management Amplify 55 Washington Street, 8th Floor Brooklyn, NY 11201 amplify.com To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to enterprise-support+unsubscribe@clever.com.

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Zarin Zarin Sultana Senior Customer Success Manager [image: Clever Icon Logo] Visit our Help Center and Clever Academy to learn more about Clever!

Description: Hi there, I am the main developer from District Management Group responsible for writing a secure sync job to merge Clever student data into our database, and I have a few questions about Secure Sync that I would like your help with! 1. Before the start of a school year, students' grades will increase by one. How do we know when that will happen, or we have to coordinate that with the district? I see that Sections have a link to Term, but that's not on the Student record, so we cannot depend on that. (For your info, our program cannot passively wait for that to happen and simply update everyone's grade, since a new Academic Year for us requires a completely new setup) 2. In the Clever Data API 3.0, the query has some kind of "record per page" limit (default 100), but I don't see an output for the number of total records for a given query. Is there a way to get that? 3. I want to sanity-check our application's secure sync architecture with you before we start writing code, in case that's the wrong way to go about it at all: - Goal: run a full sync daily and to add/update/delete our application's students, classrooms, and grades. - We will not leverage the Events API at this stage, and we do not need to sync any other data. - The overall architecture follows the ETL paradigm (extract, transform, load): - *Extract*: we call the Clever Data API 3.0 POST requests, page by page, until we get all of 3 clever tables of Students, Sections, and Teachers. We store a carbon copy of the results in staging tables on our side. - *Transform*: from the staging tables, we use our best effort to map the Clever Students, Grades, Teachers, and Sections into our app's "student", "grade" and "classroom". This will contain the bulk of the logic as our grades are different, and we have no concept of Sections, just a single "homeroom" for a student. We store the attempted transform result in a second staging table, one row per student. - *Load*: During the first few syncs, the second staging table will be reviewed by our team before it is loaded into our system. Once the process produces stable results, the load will automatically every day, except for rows marked with transformation errors. - The staging records are deleted within a short timeframe (eg. 7 days) Is this more or less the right direction, and is it similar to how other clients do it too? Does anything jump out to you as atypical, or brittle design? Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. Description: Hi PE Team! I am copying a message sent from McKenzie via our Instructure and Clever Slack channel; can you please take a look? Thanks! Hello Clever friends! We're working on a case for Elk City School District 6 where they have students being archived in our system. This has been documented for our engineers who investigated and found: "Clever deletes and re-creates this district's records under the same api_ids (not a rekey). we poll Clever once a day at 07:00 UTC. Delete+Create events with no changes in the same sync cancel themselves out. But here, the Clever change window and the MC event sync window happens to be overlapping. We pull the Delete events, there's no Create yet, so the pipeline ingests them as :explicit_delete. Seconds later Clever would expose the Create events but it's too late, those are ingested in the next day's sync. Where we see reactivation (un-archive). That's "self-healing" because those records are resolved by secondary but there's one full day where they are deleted. unless support runs a manual full sync." Can your team assist us in finding a solution for this? -- Kristina Cruz (she/her) Principal Customer Success Manager Get the most out of Clever with the new Clever Academy training course for application partners. Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, JenniferPluma Application Success Team @ Clever *Jennifer Pluma, M. Ed. (she/her)* Customer Success Manager

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Masiel Masiel Bautista (she/her) Customer Success Manager Visit our Help Center and Clever Academy to learn more about Clever!

Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Peter Ellerkamp Senior Customer Success Manager

We've designed the system so that each customer/district has a specific URI so that when users are properly assigned to their own district. If it helps, here is how we've set up our application. Our primary application is a service provider behind a standard Keycloak service, which acts as an intermediate identity provider (IdP). Keycloak allows us to support OIDC and SAML integrations with any number of customers. Each customer is assigned their own Keycloak realm which can be configured with their IdP of choice. As a practical example, if we had two districts, "district-a" (id=1234) and "district-b" (id=1235), we might use endpoints similar to this: Application endpoint: https://portal.mometrixelibrary.com/?__acct=1234 Authentication endpoint (keycloak): https://auth.mometrixelibrary.com/realms/1234-district-a/protocol/openid-connect/auth Application endpoint: https://portal.mometrixelibrary.com/?__acct=1235 Authentication endpoint (keycloak): https://auth.mometrixelibrary.com/realms/1235-district-b/protocol/openid-connect/auth As you can see each endpoint uniquely identifies the district being accessed. We are open to any recommendations you may have to help with this integration. Please let us know if there's more information we can give to explain the situation more clearly. Thanks for your help. Description: Hi Shaun and Clever PE, I'd like to introduce you to Dan Horton from Benchmark, copied here. Dan brought up some difficulties with Palm Beach last year and we just want to make sure all goes smoothly this year. To summarize the issue last year: The issue with Palm Beach revolves around a deactivation problem that resulted in duplicate classes appearing in Benchmark Education Company's system. During a Christmas break, Palm Beach introduced entirely new classes. Although the source data in January reflected only these new classes, Benchmark's system showed both the old and new classes, indicating that the old ones were not properly deactivated. This led to duplicate classes from both the first and second semesters. Palm Beach utilizes two terms in Clever: a full-year term and a semester-one term. The core of the problem is that all reporting data is managed at a classroom level. If students are moved, or a class is no longer shared, and a new class instance is created due to a change in SIS ID or Clever ID, it disrupts the ability to maintain consistent data throughout the school year. Benchmark archives its classes only at the end of its full-year term. This practice conflicts with districts like Palm Beach, which may have multiple terms or make changes mid-year, leading to discrepancies in class data and deactivation issues. Simply ending a Clever term might not generate the necessary deactivation events, contributing to these problems. Dan, I will let you add more if I'm forgetting anything! We were hoping for some advice: 1. Shaun, if you may be able to provide insights into Palm Beach's data this year and if we see anything that indicates that something similar may happen 2. PE, any advice on avoiding duplicate classes Thanks so much! FLVS would like to configure an SSO connection from our Full Time District's SIS to Clever. In order for this SSO connection to be a direct passthrough, where students do not have to enter credentials on a login page, we need Clever to support Open ID Connect as the IDP. Here is the background information driving this request. Our FLVS Full Time District and Schools uses FOCUS as the SIS. Earlier this year we implemented a Clever District Portal, https://clever.com/in/flvsfulltimepublicschools, which each of our three schools, Elementary, Middle, and High School use. Because our students start their school day by logging into FOCUS first, the decision was made by our District Leaders that the path for students to access Clever would be from their FOCUS landing page. When a student wants to access Clever, they click the Clever icon on their FOCUS landing page, which directs them to a Clever login page. Once the student enters their credentials they are directed to the appropriate schools Clever Portal. Currently, the SSO connection from FOCUS to Clever is using the LDAP protocol. This protocol does not support a direct SSO pass-through, which is why the students are presented with the Clever login page. FLVS would prefer a pass-through straight into Clever from FOCUS, but in order to enable that functionality, Clever will need to be able to support Open ID Connect as the IDP. Please let me know what the future looks like for Open ID Connect and Clever. Thank you very much for the support. Description: Hi Cara, Lisa & team - I spoke with our Partner Engineering team for some ideas on what we can do about the extra sections that appear for teachers in Prodigy. Something that may work is setting up Data Errors or Data Warnings (the linked article explains how a District Admin will see this). Especially if there is a general consensus that the only sections that should be allowed are those with subject "language, math, homeroom, etc". Some notes/caveats around the differences between data errors and data warnings: - Warnings will flag to the district admins and it will be on district admins to update and clear out the warnings. - Errors will disallow any records not meeting the criteria from even being shared with the app, so Prodigy won't see them on the API and the teachers won't see them downstream in Prodigy. - The bigger concern with setting up an error is that it becomes a hard requirement that's only adjustable by PE. so if they're confident that they only want ELA and Math subject sections for ex, then they shouldn't run into any issues. but if they want science, social studies, etc., down the line then we (PE) would have to update the data rule for them. - If the main concern is end user confusion, it might be best to start with a warning, and have the Prodigy team relay to districts that they don't want all that data. - If the concern is a technical limitation or many districts that are unwilling to change sharing permissions, then the error might make more sense, since it's creating a hard requirement. This would also remove friction between any districts who don't easily change their sharing permissions and Prodigy, so no one would really need to change much. - For anyone that loses access, districts would need to update the sharing rules or sections in Clever to match the new requirement. If you'd a call to discuss further to see if this could work, I've included our Partner Engineering team here and Katie will be able to hop on a call with your team. Description: Hi, I have some engineering questions about the way that apps are presented in the library.  I'm not sure to whom such questions should be directed, but this mailbox is the only one I've seen that seems remotely appropriate - at least it has something to do with library integration.  If there's a better target for such questions, I'd be most appreciative if you could let me know, and I'd be more than happy to send my questions there instead. --------------------------------------- Anyway, here goes: We at Worktour have recently gone live in the app library, and are now keen to deal with polishing and optimising our presence there. We've looked at the list of tags as recommended in your docs here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a9RW2b5E9aovnNgVv7-n5DTbSiCS7nGH1zGusmrsT34/edit?gid=0#gid=0 *Question 1:* Is there a complete list of currently-used tags available, ideally with associated search statistics?  None of the tags in the above spreadsheet is likely to be appropriate for an app like ours which straddles across subject matter domains, and we don't want to waste our budget of ten tags on terms which nobody ever actually searches, even if they may be accurately descriptive of our product. We currently have the following tags specified.  We appreciate that this is not necessarily a very cleverly-selected set, but given the limit of ten tags it's important for us to understand how the end user would interact with the library and what search results are likely to be returned given any given user query. I've been experimenting with search results for different search terms and am confused as to how we could be getting the results that we're seeing.  Our app is concerned with careers and giving students virtual tours of workplaces.  As you can see from the tag list above, we have three tags which explicitly mention careers, namely "career", "career plan" and "career readiness". For these tests, I've logged in as the test user "teacher1/clever" here: https://clever.com/in/library-test/teacher/resourceHub and our "Worktour" app has been installed.  I used the "teacher1" test account because I don't (knowingly) have any ability to get to the library logging in as myself (please do feel free to disabuse me of any ignorance I may be evincing!), so when using teacher1 I'm on ground that's been well-trodden before. Now we get to my experiments and questions.  I searched for "career" and got these results: I notice that our app doesn't appear at all.  I would have expected it at least to appear in the list of "Your resources", since it's installed.  I appreciate that this test user has a lot of apps installed, but there appear to be ~250 apps in the library (counting by stepping through the unfiltered pages of the library), and I wouldn't expect there would be all that many concerning careers.  I could easily be wrong, but there's no scroll bar or ellipses in the "Your resources" list to suggest that there are (or could be) more search hits potentially out there. *Question 2:* Were I a normal teacher-type user with fewer resources installed, would I have seen our app appear on the basis of this search term, in either of the "Your resources" or "New resources you can try" categories?  Why? Ok, so I now tried "careers", and got completely different results. This is very strange, since it suggests that (at least?) the tags on apps are not being stemmified for search. *Question 3a:*  Are tags stemmified in the search or not? *Question 3b: *What about other indexed content such as the product description? If there's no stemification of tags (or elsewhere?), as would appear to be the case, then it would suggest that we need to be very careful in our selection of the very characters and parts of speech mentioned in our tags.  This might be easier if we could get some search term frequency data, but on the face of it I'd never have guessed that our app would get no hits at all for "careers". Presumably, this can't have been caused by our maxing out the real estate for the result set because we only got back one hit in the "Your resources" box, whereas it's clear from the first search that the UI is prepared to show at least three hits in this result box. To try to understand the stemification issue more, I tried another experiment in which I searched for a word which I knew to be in our product description, but expected to be rare or absent in any other app, namely "hygienist".  Searching for this, I got this result: Great, we appear in the search results, but still unclear why this doesn't appear in "Your resources".  Next i tried searching for "hygienists" (note the plural).  This gave us these results: OK, so Worktour still appears, but now we get a hit for WriteReader.  I took a look at the product page for this and can find no instance of either "hygienist" or "hygienists". *Question 4:*  Can you explain these search results?  This clearly has nothing to do with tags. Next, I searched for "career plan" which is another one of our tags (see above), but this time it's much more specific. In this case, I got a result in the "New resources you can try" result box.  This is a little bit strange because it's already installed, so its a little odd that it's suggesting that I try it out, but I'm never going to complain about getting such placement in the "New resources yo can try" box, unless other people are getting impressions instead of us, of course.  However, the fact that we didn't get a search hit in the "Your resources" box is decidedly strange.  This is one of our tags spelled verbatim, and there's only one hit in the "Your resources" result box, so the result set can't be omitting Worktour because of being truncated. I've looked at the "College & Career Exploration Platform" app, which appears in the result set shown above, and the word "plan" doesn't seem to appear anywhere in the product description, so I don't understand why our app isn't appearing and this one is. *Question 5a:* Can you explain this search behaviour? *Question 5b:* Is there something different about multi-word tags that makes them less applicable or have lower search rank? Next, I searched explicitly for the name of our product, "Worktour". In this case I did get a hit for our app appearing in the "Your resources" box, so it's clearly possible for us to get placement there, but I don't understand why we appear there and not for other searches which seem more than specific enough to have forced our app into that result box. This all almost feels as if tags are not indexed at all, and that the search results are based only on other parts of the content, but that seems like too much of an oversight to be plausible, even though it's consistent with the above observations. *Question 6a:* Are tags indexed for keyword search? *Question 6b:* If so, how do I understand the above search results, and if not what are tags good for? Perhaps tags are just some sort of UI affordance for the teacher user to look at after landing on the the product details page. Perhaps they show up in some analytics I haven't been able to find yet.  It doesn't seem to be possible to filter by them on the advanced library filter options. Sorry to pepper you with these questions.  I expect that they ought to be trivial for someone in-the-know to answer.  I appreciate that we still need to do a bunch of typing and tweaking to show our product in the best possible light.  We're just trying to understand the way that the underlying system works so as to be able to do so. Many thanks in advance, Lydia. -- You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "integrations" group. Description: My organization, 3DE, has a custom middleware that we are piloting with Fort Wayne Community Schools. We use Clever to connect educators in participating districts with our LMS, d2L. We have full modules in d2L that educators are accessing, and many use links to specific pages/modules in our instance of d2L to point students quickly to the correct page for the day. I received the following email from a teacher and am wondering if what she requests is possible and, if so, what needs to be done: "“Since 3DE’s change to Clever, the direct links to specific modules in 3DE’s d2L no longer work for students unless they have already signed into 3DE in another browser tab. Is there a way to configure SSO so that a student can: 1. Click a direct link I provide them to a specific resource in 3DE’s d2L; 2. Be authenticated through SSO if they are not already signed in; and 3. Automatically be directed to the specific page/resource that was linked by me? Canva is one of the apps that was recently added as a link through Clever. When students click on a direct link to a Canva page without already being signed into Clever, they are directed to Clever to authenticate and then are taken directly to the linked Canva page. That is the type of experience I am hoping we could create with the 3DE links as well. Instead, when students click a direct link I provide them to a module in 3DE’s d2L, they are directed to the 3DE d2L login page and are asked to provide a username and password (no SSO) I’m hoping there may be a way for the direct 3DE links to work more like the Canva links—where Clever authenticates the student and then passes them directly to the specific page they were trying to access." Thanks - Rebecca

Description: Hi Brent & Rachel, I'm glad we were able to connect today about a few potential areas for improvement. I have compiled our responses and a few resources in the following categories: *Optimizing API Calls: Quick answers* 1. Bulk contacts for multiple students? No, we don't have a batch /mycontactsendpoint. You can use GET /users?role=contact&limit=10000 and match contacts to students with student_relationships. 2. Rate limit / concurrency? It's 1,200 requests per minute per token. If you get a 429error, wait and retry. We don’t publish a concurrency number. You shouldn’t need much parallelism if you use the bulk contacts call. 3. Contacts inline on the student roster (expand / include)? No, /schools/{id}/users does not return contacts and there is no expand/include parameter. 4. SFTP / bulk export with contacts already joined? We don't offer this for apps at this time. SFTP is how districts send data into Clever. You’d still join contacts from GET /users?role=contact to your student roster. 5. Does the Events payload include contact data? Description: Hi there, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted. The following endpoints will be sunsetted: - GET /contacts - GET /contacts/{id} - GET /contacts/{id}/students - GET /contacts/{id}/district - GET /students/{id}/mycontacts - GET /events?record_type=contacts To avoid service interruptions, you'll need to upgrade your integration to use API v3.x Contacts. We're making this change because: - v2.x Contacts only support a single relationship per contact, which can result in inaccurate or incomplete data. - v3.x Contacts allow for multiple distinct relationships per student, leading to better data accuracy, improved reliability, and stronger security. To support your migration, we recommend reviewing the following pages from our developer documentation, which provide more details on this change: - Migrating from API v2.x Contacts to v3.x Contacts - Contacts & Guardians Please reply to this email by May 2nd with: - Your planned migration timeline - Any blockers or questions we can help with We’re here to support you through the upgrade—let us know how we can help! Best, Masiel Masiel Bautista (she/her) Customer Success Manager Visit our Help Center and Clever Academy to learn more about Clever!

This creates a conflict, since OAuth authorization responses require an HTTPS endpoint, while native app deep links cannot serve as OAuth callbacks. Could you please clarify: Whether Clever supports separate values for: OAuth callback URL App launch / deep-link URL If not, whether there are plans to support this distinction for native applications (as other providers do). Whether Clever’s intended approach for native apps is to use a web intermediary to handle OAuth and then redirect to the app. I may be misunderstanding Clever’s expected flow, so I would greatly appreciate confirmation from someone familiar with Clever’s OAuth and SSO design. Thank you for your time. I would be happy to schedule a quick call with a tech representative to help clarify the issue.

Description: Hi Melissa, This is a reminder that Clever will be sunsetting all API v2.x Contacts endpoints on July 31, 2025. After this date, these endpoints will no longer be accessible, and any integrations still relying on them will be disrupted.
